issues.legal_issue: A sale of immovable property that must be made by registered instrument is not complete for purposes of a pre-emption demand until registration of the instrument is complete, even if the instrument, once registered, operates from an earlier date.
material_facts: The parties accepted that the pre-emption right arose only from a valid, complete and bona fide sale, and that the first demand had to be made after completion of the sale.
The sale concerned a house and was made by an instrument that was required to be registered.
The pre-emptor made the first demand after the instrument was executed and presented for registration, but before it was copied into the registration records, when registration became complete.
The instrument stated that it would operate from the date of execution; the court held that this did not make the sale complete before registration was complete.
issues.conclusion: The sale was complete only when registration was complete. Because the first pre-emption demand was made earlier, it was premature and the pre-emption suit failed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, a sale of tangible immovable property of the relevant value can be made only by a registered instrument. Sections 60 and 61 of the Registration Act govern completion of registration, and section 61 provides that registration is complete when the prescribed endorsements and certificate are copied into the register. Section 47 permits a registered document to operate from the time it would have operated had registration not been required, but does not determine when the sale is completed; retrospective operation does not make the sale complete before registration is complete. The first demand under the applicable law of pre-emption must follow completion of the sale. The court approved Tilakdhari Singh v. Gour Narain, Nareshchandra Datta v. Gireeshchandra Das, and Gobardhan Bar v. Guna Dhar Bar, and distinguished Bindeshri v. Somnath Bhadry and Gopal Ram v. Lachmi Misir.

predicates.preemption_proceeding: A claimant brought a proceeding to enforce a right of pre-emption arising from a sale.
predicates.sale_requires_registered_instrument: The sale concerned immovable property for which the applicable law required a registered instrument.
predicates.first_demand_preceded_registration_compl: The pre-emptor made the first demand before the instrument was copied into the registration records and registration was complete.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption proceeding concerns a sale requiring a registered instrument and the first demand came before registration was complete, the pre-emption claim fails.
